messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Canary deployment for model 'redwood-chat-beta' (canary_id=c-17) seeing 12% 5xx from EU region and elevated tail latency. Auto-fallbacks triggered to fallback-legacy variant. Dashboard: <https://dashboard.redwood/alerts/2167894321>
maya: i’m on it. paging @aj and @dana oncall. what’s the customer impact?
aj: seeing spike in 503s and some requests stuck in retry loops. support-bot flagged 3 paying customers in EU experiencing degraded responses.
dana: confirm — our synthetic check against the canary shows 200->500 oscillation: some requests go to v2, then fallback to legacy, then get routed back to canary because sticky routing cookie TTL mismatch. looks like sticky affinity TTL was set to 0 for the canary in eu-west-1 which is causing immediate re-eval and oscillation.
lee: any error logs? paste a snippet?
maya: logs show model variant mismatch errors right before the 5xx. snippet:
```
E 03:12:08 routing: route_request id=abc123 user=acct-55 policy=smart-routing fallback=enabled
E 03:12:08 executor: selected_variant=v2 expected_variant=v2
E 03:12:08 fallback: sticky_affinity_ttl=0, eval-> fallback-> route_recalc
E 03:12:09 model-server eu-west-1 v-legacy: 500 InternalServerError "kv-cache corruption"
E 03:12:10 routing: re-evaluating route -> selected_variant=v2 (canary)
E 03:12:11 model-server eu-west-1 v2: OOM allocating kv-cache
```
maya: that sequence looks like canary sometimes fails OOM on v2, fallback lands on legacy which errors due to kv-cache corruption, sticky ttl=0 then immediately retries back to canary -> loop.
aj: that explains retry loop and high p99. customers get a mix of 500s and long waits.
dana: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause canary rollout (prevent new traffic to c-17) 2) change fallback policy from sticky to immediate fallback->baseline (no retry) 3) extend sticky TTL to a stable value so we don't oscillate 4) scale up v2 kv-cache memory in eu-west. which do we do first?
maya: priority is stop customer impact. pause canary and change fallback policy. i'll do pause + trigger a controlled rollback to baseline. aj, apply policy change to disable sticky for canaries in eu-west while we investigate.
aj: on it. running command to pause rollout:
```
# pause canary rollout
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 https://control.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/c-17/pause
```
aj: done — API returned 200 and rollout state is PAUSED. new requests should not be routed to canary for incoming traffic.
dana: switching fallback policy now to no-sticky for canary->baseline in eu-west: applying policy patch.
```
# policy patch
kubectl -n routing patch configmap smart-routing-policy --type merge -p '{"eu-west-1": {"canary": {"fallback":"baseline","sticky":false}}}'
```
lee: policy patched and pushed. routing service reloaded config.
maya: confirm with a few synthetic checks.
support-bot: running customer synthetic tests for affected accounts... 3/3 now reporting success within baseline latencies. alert suppressed.
aj: i still see some tail errors in logs from older in-flight requests, but rate is down to normal.
dana: ops notes — sticky TTL 0 was introduced by a deploy two days ago as part of experiment EXP-439 to try immediate variant switch for AB tests. looks like the experiment unintentionally targeted canaries in eu-west.
maya: can we roll back that config change globally? we should revert the experiment targeting and add a guard so TTL=0 cannot be applied to canaries.
aj: i'll add a validation check in the rollout service to reject sticky_ttl < 30s for canaries. filing a quick PR.
dana: for root cause, we should pair the OOM on v2 with kv-cache corruption on legacy. they combined to produce the loop. scheduling postmortem; assign owners for model memory tuning and legacy kv-cache fix.
lee: action items: 1) aj: validation for sticky TTL for canaries (PR+deploy) 2) dana: investigate kv-cache corruption on legacy variant (investigate dumps + repro) 3) maya: run a controlled canary re-run with increased kv-cache memory and monitoring hooks 4) support: notify affected customers with incident summary + ETA.
support-bot: draft message ready for customer emails.
maya: sending customer notice now, note included rollback and ETA for full remediation.
dana: i'll keep the thread open for postmortem notes. thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup:
maya: closing page — will reopen if we see reappearance.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, mitigation=canary_paused+fallback_policy_change, severity=sev2. Postmortem due in 48h. <https://dashboard.redwood/incidents/2167894321/postmortem>"
